_register: Polite but plain: address the reader with 您 only where a sentence must speak to them directly, otherwise leave the subject out (impersonal); buttons, menu entries and step lists use short verb phrases without 请 (借出, 保存, 扫描条码), and 请 only at the start of a sentence that asks the reader to do something; no jokes, no exclamation marks (！), no colloquial particles (吧, 哦, 啦).
_quotes: Use the Chinese quotation marks “ ” (U+201C/U+201D) for quoted text and ‘ ’ for a quote inside a quote (「 」 is Traditional-Chinese and Japanese practice, not used); use full-width punctuation (，。：；？) in Chinese sentences but keep ASCII punctuation next to Latin text, numbers and placeholders; no space between Chinese characters; put one space between Chinese text and Latin letters or digits only where the English source has a word there (e.g. 使用 ISBN 查找, 共 {{count}} 册); keep → and the product names (BiblioViva, Tailscale, rclone, Koha, SBN, OPAC, Docker, Raspberry Pi, Wi-Fi, ISBN, CSV, PDF) as they are.
_plural: Chinese has no plural forms, so every plural selector needs only the form `other`; a number is followed by a counter: 册 for copies and books (3 册), 条 for records (12 条记录), 位 for patrons, students and teachers (5 位读者), 个 for classes and general things, 张 for cards and slips (2 张读者证), 次 for times.

copy.note: One physical copy with its own barcode (counter 册). Chinese library systems also say 馆藏 for the holdings as a whole, but 复本 is the plain word for one copy of a title; never 副本 (that means a duplicate file).

record.note: The catalogue entry of a title, as in Chinese library systems (书目数据); short form 记录 where the context is clear. One record has one or more 复本.

patron.note: The standard word in Chinese libraries and library software (读者证, 读者管理); never 用户 or 借阅者.

card.note: The library card of a patron; short form 借书证 is older and not used, 卡 only in 打印读者证.

loan.note: The action and the record of lending; on buttons and in the desk text the verb is 借出 (lend) and 借阅 as the noun/area name (借阅记录).

return.note: The action: 归还 on the menu and buttons; the area as a whole is 借还 (借阅与归还).

renew.note: Extending the due date; the word used in every Chinese library system.

due date.note: The date by which the copy must be back.

overdue.note: Past the due date; 超期 is also used but 逾期 is plainer in software.

reminder.note: The printed slip asking for the return (催还单 as the name of the printed slip); 催还 is the verb.

call number.note: The shelf mark on the spine, as in all Chinese libraries (B 4 DEL, 590 ROS); never 排架号 or 书架号.

spine band.note: The coloured band on the spine with pictogram and call number; 书脊标识带 is longer and not used.

label.note: An adhesive label with a barcode: 条码标签 where the barcode must be stressed.

barcode.note: Mainland usage in libraries and retail; 条形码 is the longer form of the same word, not used. Written 条码, without a space before a number.

class.note: A school class (3 B); counter 个. Single class name written as in the data, e.g. 3 B.

group.note: Used for a group of teachers (教师组); 小组 only in running text.

reading level.note: The school year a book is meant for; in Chinese schools 适读年级 (suitable grade) is also said, but 阅读等级 follows the name of the setting in the app.

genre.note: How fiction is sorted (小说, 诗歌…); 类型 is more usual for films and games, so 体裁 is used for books.

classification.note: The sorting scheme (the app uses Dewey for non-fiction; Chinese libraries usually use 中图法, so keep 分类法 for 'classification scheme' and name Dewey as 杜威十进分类法).

catalogue.note: The library catalogue (馆藏目录); the area of the app is 编目 (cataloguing) only where the English says 'cataloguing'.

stocktaking.note: Checking the shelves against the catalogue, usually 馆藏盘点; never 清点 or 库存 (that means stock in commerce).

wish list.note: Books a patron would like the library to have; the standard word in Chinese libraries is 读者荐购 (荐购清单 for the list, 荐购书目).

census.note: Registering patrons with their photo (读者信息采集); 普查 is not used, since it suggests a national census.

class upgrade.note: Moving every class up a year at the end of the school year (3 B becomes 4 B); 升级 is the verb, 升班 is not used.

anonymise.note: Erase the personal data of a patron for good; the action on the button is 匿名化处理 in running text.

staff account.note: A shared login per role; 账户 (not 帐户) is the current standard written form.

restore.note: Putting a backup back (恢复备份); 还原 is also used but 恢复 is the usual word in software.

print list.note: A list of patrons or copies to print cards or labels for; 打印 (not 列印, which is Taiwan usage).

scanner.note: The USB barcode reader that types like a keyboard; in text 条码扫描枪 on first mention. Never 扫描仪 (that is a document or flatbed scanner).

wizard.note: The first-start sequence of questions; short form 向导.

demo data.note: The invented school the program can fill itself with; 演示数据 is also understood.

student.note: Counter 位 when counted politely, 名 in lists; use 位 in the app for consistency with 读者.

teacher.note: Formal and plain word used in schools; 老师 is spoken and not used in the interface.

administration.note: The area for administrators: 系统管理 where the English means 'Administration' as a menu entry and 管理员 for the person.

configuration.note: The settings of the installation (系统配置); 设置 for a single option or page of options in running text.

note.note: A free-text note on a record or patron; 笔记 is not used.

return desk / circulation desk.note: The desk where loans and returns are handled (also 流通台 in library science, which is less plain); the area as a whole is 借阅.
